newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt allows more time for Alamein BOT airport.
newsitem.headline: Egypt allows more time for Alamein BOT airport.

text.p: The Egyptian Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) said on Saturday it was postponing until January 30 the opening of bids for a BOT (build-operate-transfer) airport at El Alamein on the northwest coast.
The CAA originally invited bids for the project in September and the previous date for opening them was December 31. The authority gave no reason for the delay.
The international airport at El Alamein, site of the World War Two battle, is meant as a convenient landing-point for tourists vsiting the beaches of the Mediterranean coast.
The project has fallen behind Egypt's other proposed BOT airport at Marsa Alam on the Red Sea coast.

The authoritative magazine MEED said this week that the CAA had selected the Kuwaiti company Mohamed Abdulmuhsin Kharafi and Sons for negotiations on the Marsa Alam airport, which is expected to cost about 120 million pounds ($35 million).
The company that builds the airport will probably have the right to operate it for between 25 and 30 years before ownership reverts to the Egyptian state, MEED said.
